playIdeas.title: Soft treasure basket
playIdeas.summary: Offer a few safe household textures to explore together.
steps: Place the items in the container.
Sit nearby and let your child choose what to touch.
Name textures calmly as they explore.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A low-mess, gently engaging pause with very little setup. Stay nearby, offer simple guidance, and let your child explore at their own pace.
playIdeas.parentNote: Use only what feels easy to gather; two textures can be plenty.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use only large, clean items that cannot be swallowed.

playIdeas.title: Couch cushion tunnel
playIdeas.summary: Make a small tunnel for crawling, peeking, or passing a toy through.
steps: Place cushions on the floor with a low open space between them.
Invite your child to crawl, peek, or pass the toy through.
Stay nearby and change the tunnel if it starts to wobble.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Expect more movement and a little room reset afterward. Join for a few minutes, then keep the tunnel as simple as your space allows.
playIdeas.parentNote: A short setup can turn familiar furniture into a fresh play space.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep the tunnel low, stable, and away from sharp furniture edges.

playIdeas.title: Kitchen spoon rhythm
playIdeas.summary: Tap gentle patterns with safe kitchen items.
steps: Place the bowl on a tea towel to soften the sound.
Tap a slow pattern and pause for your child to answer.
Try quiet taps, soft scrapes, and gentle beats.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: It can become lively, but the setup stays small and easy to put away. Keep the rhythm soft and join only as much as feels good.
playIdeas.parentNote: Keep the sound level comfortable for everyone nearby.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use sturdy, clean items and supervise while your child holds the spoon.

playIdeas.title: Laundry color sorting
playIdeas.summary: Sort a small pile of clean laundry by color or type.
steps: Choose a small pile of clean laundry.
Pick one simple sorting idea, like socks and shirts or light and dark.
Let your child place each item in a basket.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A low-mess way to turn a familiar chore into a small shared moment. Stay close, name what you notice, and let the sorting stay imperfect.
playIdeas.parentNote: It is fine if the sorting is imperfect; keep the moment easy.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Avoid items with loose cords, small parts, or laundry products nearby.

playIdeas.title: Window weather watch
playIdeas.summary: Look outside and talk about what you notice.
steps: Sit or stand together near a window.
Point to one thing you notice outside.
Use short calm words like cloudy, bright, windy, or quiet.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quiet, low-mess pause for a full day. Offer a few words, follow your child's attention, and let the window do most of the work.
playIdeas.parentNote: Even thirty seconds of noticing can soften the pace.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep windows locked and supervise closely.

playIdeas.title: Sticker rescue
playIdeas.summary: Place a few stickers on paper and invite your child to peel them away.
steps: Place a few large stickers on the paper with one edge slightly lifted.
Invite your child to peel each sticker and move it somewhere new.
Talk about where each sticker lands.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A focused table moment with a little peel-and-place curiosity. Set out only a few stickers so the activity stays light.
playIdeas.parentNote: Starting with two or three stickers keeps the choice gentle.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use large stickers and keep small backing pieces out of reach.

playIdeas.title: Pillow path
playIdeas.summary: Lay pillows on the floor for stepping, crawling, or balancing with help.
steps: Place pillows in a short path on the floor.
Hold your child's hand if they want support.
Try stepping, crawling, or moving a soft toy along the path.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A more active idea for a moment when you can join in closely. Keep the path short so it feels playful, not like a big setup.
playIdeas.parentNote: Adjust the path to your energy and the space you already have.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use a clear floor area and stop if pillows start to slide.

playIdeas.title: Quiet book basket
playIdeas.summary: Set out a small basket of books for a calm shared pause.
steps: Place a few books in a basket within easy reach.
Let your child choose one book.
Look at pictures, name one detail, or sit quietly together.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A low-effort, low-mess pause when everyone needs something softer. Let your child choose the pace, even if that means only looking at one page.
playIdeas.parentNote: This can be a calm pause, not a full reading session.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use sturdy books without torn pages or loose pieces for younger children.

playIdeas.title: Soft scarf peekaboo
playIdeas.summary: Use a light scarf or cloth for a gentle peekaboo moment.
steps: Sit close where your baby can see your face.
Hold the scarf near your face and lower it slowly.
Pause, smile, and repeat only while it feels welcome.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A soft, low-mess way to share attention with almost no preparation. Keep your voice gentle and stop whenever your baby seems ready for a break.
playIdeas.parentNote: One slow peek can be just right.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep fabric away from your baby's nose and mouth and supervise closely.

playIdeas.title: Container matching
playIdeas.summary: Match safe lids and containers from the kitchen.
steps: Set out two or three clean containers and lids.
Show one lid and wonder aloud where it might fit.
Let your child try matches, stack pieces, or simply explore.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quiet kitchen activity with easy cleanup. Matching may turn into stacking or sorting, and that still fits the moment.
playIdeas.parentNote: Let the containers be interesting without needing a correct answer.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use clean, lightweight items without sharp edges or small loose parts.

playIdeas.title: Towel road
playIdeas.summary: Fold a towel into a soft road for small toys or cars.
steps: Fold a towel into a long strip on the floor.
Place one small toy at the start of the road.
Invite your child to move the toy slowly, quickly, or around a bend.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A low-mess pretend setup that can last one minute or longer. Narrate softly, then let your child take the road wherever it goes.
playIdeas.parentNote: A towel can become a road, river, bridge, or path.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep the towel flat so it does not become a tripping spot.

playIdeas.title: Sock puppet hello
playIdeas.summary: Turn a clean sock into a simple hello puppet.
steps: Put a clean sock over your hand.
Make the puppet say hello in a soft voice.
Pause and let your child answer, point, or simply watch.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A small connection moment shaped by your gentle participation. Keep the voice simple and follow your child's response.
playIdeas.parentNote: The puppet does not need a story; a tiny hello is enough.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use a clean sock without loose threads or small decorations.

playIdeas.title: Gentle animal walks
playIdeas.summary: Move like quiet animals across a small safe space.
steps: Choose one gentle animal, like a cat, turtle, or bear.
Move slowly across the room together.
Try a quiet version and a slightly bigger version.
Rest when the movement feels done.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A movement idea that does not need a big setup. Join for a few rounds, then let the pace soften when the room feels ready.
playIdeas.parentNote: Quiet animals can still be playful.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Clear the floor and avoid fast movement near furniture.

playIdeas.title: Water brush painting
playIdeas.summary: Paint temporary marks with water on cardboard or an outdoor surface.
steps: Pour a small amount of water into a bowl.
Show how the brush makes a mark on cardboard or patio.
Let your child make lines, dots, or soft shapes.
Watch the marks fade as they dry.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Creative, temporary marks without paint or lasting cleanup. Stay close with the water bowl and keep the activity small.
playIdeas.parentNote: Fading marks can be part of the calm rhythm.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use only a little water and choose a non-slippery surface.

playIdeas.title: Spoon and cup transfer
playIdeas.summary: Move dry items from one cup to another with a spoon.
neededItems: Large dry pasta or cotton balls
steps: Place a few large dry items in one cup.
Show how to scoop one item with the spoon.
Invite your child to move items to the other cup.
Pause whenever the table needs a quick reset.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A focused table activity where a little cleanup may happen. Use only a handful of items so it stays manageable.
playIdeas.parentNote: Spills are part of the activity and can be kept small.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Choose items that are safe for your child's age and supervise closely.

playIdeas.title: Laundry texture naming
playIdeas.summary: Touch clean laundry together and name how it feels.
steps: Choose two or three clean laundry items.
Offer one item at a time.
Use simple words like soft, warm, smooth, or bumpy.
Let your child touch, hold, or look.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A gentle sensory pause with almost no setup. Name one or two textures, then let the laundry return to the day.
playIdeas.parentNote: You can do this while folding or sitting nearby.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Avoid items with loose strings, buttons, or small parts.

playIdeas.title: Shadow watching
playIdeas.summary: Notice simple shadows on a wall, floor, or curtain.
steps: Find a place where a shadow is easy to see.
Point to one shadow and name it simply.
Move your hand slowly and notice what changes.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quiet observation moment for a slower part of the day. Stay curious, keep it brief, and follow what your child notices.
playIdeas.parentNote: No setup is needed if the light is already there.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Avoid looking directly at bright sunlight.

playIdeas.title: Blanket toy rescue
playIdeas.summary: Hide part of a toy under a blanket and invite a gentle rescue.
steps: Place a soft toy partly under the blanket.
Say that the toy is waiting to be found.
Let your child lift the blanket or point to the toy.
Celebrate softly and try again if they want.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A small shared rescue with very little cleanup. Keep the hiding easy so it feels comforting rather than tricky.
playIdeas.parentNote: The toy can stay partly visible.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use a light blanket and keep fabric away from faces.

playIdeas.title: Tiny stuffed picnic
playIdeas.summary: Set up a small pretend picnic for stuffed animals.
steps: Lay a small cloth on the table or floor.
Invite one or two stuffed animals to sit nearby.
Offer pretend cups or plates.
Ask what the animals might like today.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Gentle pretend play with a cozy feeling. Join long enough to start the scene, then let your child lead the picnic.
playIdeas.parentNote: One animal and one cup can carry the whole picnic.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use unbreakable cups and keep small pretend pieces away from younger children.

playIdeas.title: Soft cleanup song
playIdeas.summary: Use a short gentle tune while putting a few items away together.
steps: Choose only a few items to put away.
Hum or sing a short soft tune.
Put one item away together.
Stop after the small reset feels done.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A tiny reset becomes a connected moment without pressure. Keep the number of items small so it feels doable.
playIdeas.parentNote: Aim for a softer transition, not a perfect room.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep pathways clear and avoid rushing while carrying toys.

playIdeas.title: Paper bag discovery
playIdeas.summary: Place one safe object in a paper bag for a quiet guessing moment.
steps: Place one familiar object inside the bag.
Invite your child to feel the outside of the bag.
Offer one gentle hint if they want it.
Open the bag together.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quiet curiosity moment with almost no cleanup. Keep the object familiar so the guessing stays light.
playIdeas.parentNote: You can skip guessing and simply discover the object together.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Do not place the bag over anyone's head and use only safe objects.

playIdeas.title: Soft ball roll and pause
playIdeas.summary: Roll a soft ball back and forth with gentle pauses.
steps: Sit on the floor facing your child.
Roll the ball slowly toward them.
Pause and wait to see what they do.
Roll it again if the moment still feels good.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A low-mess connection idea with a steady rhythm. The pauses matter as much as the rolling.
playIdeas.parentNote: Your child may watch, touch, or push the ball in their own way.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use a soft ball and keep the floor clear.

playIdeas.title: Blanket boat
playIdeas.summary: Pretend a blanket on the floor is a small boat.
steps: Lay a blanket flat on the floor.
Sit beside it or place a soft toy on it.
Pretend the blanket is a boat moving slowly.
Name what you see on the gentle trip.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Pretend play feels soft and contained here. Join for the first idea, then let the boat stay as simple as your child wants.
playIdeas.parentNote: The boat can stay still; imagination can do the moving.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep the blanket flat and do not pull a child on it.

playIdeas.title: Bathroom mirror faces
playIdeas.summary: Make a few gentle faces together in the mirror.
steps: Stand together where the mirror is easy to see.
Make one gentle face, like sleepy, surprised, or happy.
Pause and let your child look or copy.
End after a few faces.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A brief, low-effort connection idea for a transition moment. Keep it soft and stop before it becomes too silly or loud.
playIdeas.parentNote: Two faces can be plenty.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep your child steady and away from wet or slippery areas.

playIdeas.title: Towel peek path
playIdeas.summary: Lay two towels on the floor for a soft path with little peek stops.
steps: Lay two towels in a short path on the floor.
Pause at each towel edge and peek underneath together.
Invite your child to step, crawl, or pat the path at their own pace.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A soft movement idea with almost no setup or cleanup. Keep the path short, pause often, and let the rhythm stay gentle.
playIdeas.parentNote: A short path can help the day move without asking much from you.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep towels flat so they do not slide or bunch under little feet.

playIdeas.title: Soft block knockdown
playIdeas.summary: Stack a small tower of soft blocks and invite an easy knockdown.
steps: Stack two or three soft blocks into a short tower.
Pause so your child can look before knocking it down.
Build it again only if the moment still feels fun.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quick burst of energy can still stay small. Keep the tower low and the reset simple.
playIdeas.parentNote: Stopping after one or two towers still counts as a good moment.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use soft blocks only and keep the tower low enough to stay safe if it tips.

playIdeas.title: Kitchen bowl nesting
playIdeas.summary: Set out a few bowls for simple stacking and nesting together.
steps: Place a few clean bowls on the floor or table.
Show one bowl resting inside another.
Let your child stack, nest, or separate them in their own way.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quiet kitchen moment with easy cleanup and familiar objects. It can stay calm even if the bowls end up spread around you.
playIdeas.parentNote: There is no need to teach the right order for the bowls.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use lightweight bowls without sharp edges and stay close during play.

playIdeas.title: Bath cup pour
playIdeas.summary: Pour small amounts of bath water from one cup to another.
steps: Offer one cup with a little water in it.
Show a slow pour into the second cup.
Let your child try pouring, filling, and pouring again.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Bath time can focus on one simple action instead of lots of stimulation. A little splashing is normal, so keep the setup small.
playIdeas.parentNote: One cup may be enough to give bath time a fresh rhythm.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Stay within arm's reach in the bath and keep the floor dry around the tub.

playIdeas.title: Couch island pretend
playIdeas.summary: Pretend the couch is a small island with safe places to land nearby.
steps: Name the couch as the island and the floor as water.
Place one pillow nearby as a safe landing spot.
Invite your child to climb, sit, and imagine a tiny island story.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Pretend play in a familiar space with only a little setup. Stay close enough to guide the movement and let the story stay simple.
playIdeas.parentNote: A short island story can feel just as satisfying as a long one.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep movement slow and supervise closely around furniture edges.

playIdeas.title: Stuffed animal bedtime
playIdeas.summary: Help a stuffed animal settle for a tiny bedtime routine.
steps: Choose one stuffed animal together.
Cover it with a cloth and say goodnight in a soft voice.
Add one tiny bedtime step, like a cuddle or a yawn.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A calm pretend moment that can gently soften a busy part of the day. Keep the routine tiny so it feels comforting, not like a task.
playIdeas.parentNote: Let the pretend routine be tiny; it does not need to mirror real bedtime.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use light fabric only and keep it away from a child's face during play.

playIdeas.title: Window bird watch
playIdeas.summary: Pause at the window and notice birds or other small outdoor movement.
steps: Stand or sit where the outside view is easy to see.
Point out one bird, flutter, or movement outdoors.
Name only what you notice and let silence be part of the moment.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A low-pressure pause for slower energy. You may only notice one small thing, and that can be plenty.
playIdeas.parentNote: No birds today is fine; clouds, branches, or passing light still work.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep windows locked and supervise closely around window areas.

playIdeas.title: Paper towel roll tunnel
playIdeas.summary: Roll small toys through a paper towel tube for a quick surprise moment.
neededItems: Small soft toy or large pom
steps: Hold the roll over a tray, table, or your hand.
Drop one toy through and listen for it to land.
Let your child take turns dropping and retrieving the toy.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A tiny repeatable activity that feels fresh with very little effort. Keep the pieces few so setup and cleanup stay easy.
playIdeas.parentNote: One roll and one toy can carry the whole activity.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use items large enough for your child's age and avoid cardboard edges that feel rough.

playIdeas.title: Sock matching basket
playIdeas.summary: Gather a few socks in a basket and look for simple pairs together.
steps: Place a few socks in a basket.
Pull out two at a time and notice color or size.
Let your child pair them, stack them, or simply sort by feel.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A familiar home task can become a calm shared moment. It still works if the pairs stay imperfect.
playIdeas.parentNote: There is no need to correct every mismatch.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use clean socks only and keep the basket light enough to move safely.

playIdeas.title: Soft toy hide and find
playIdeas.summary: Hide one soft toy in an easy spot and invite a gentle search.
steps: Choose one soft toy your child knows well.
Hide it where part of it still peeks out.
Invite your child to look, point, or pick it up.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A light search game with almost no cleanup. Keep the hiding spots easy to reach and let the toy be partly visible if that feels better.
playIdeas.parentNote: Seeing a little bit of the toy can make the game feel safer and sweeter.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Avoid hiding toys in high, tight, or hard-to-reach places.

playIdeas.title: Gentle hallway parade
playIdeas.summary: Take a slow little parade down the hallway with soft steps and simple sounds.
steps: Choose a slow walking rhythm together.
March softly down the hallway once or twice.
Add a wave, a turn, or a quiet hum if it feels fun.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A short movement break for a transition moment. Keep the parade brief and let the energy settle as you finish.
playIdeas.parentNote: One lap can be plenty when the day already feels loud.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep the hallway clear and use soft voices if others are nearby.

playIdeas.title: Picnic blanket sorting
playIdeas.summary: Sort a few safe household items onto a blanket in simple groups.
steps: Spread a blanket on the floor.
Place a few safe items beside it.
Invite your child to group them by color, size, or where they belong.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A familiar sorting moment that feels a little special on a blanket. Keep the groups loose and let curiosity lead.
playIdeas.parentNote: The blanket makes the moment feel new even if the items are ordinary.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Choose sturdy items without sharp edges or small loose pieces.

playIdeas.title: Sponge squeeze outside
playIdeas.summary: Squeeze water from a sponge outdoors for a simple sensory reset.
steps: Wet the sponge with a little water.
Show how to squeeze it over the ground or a bucket.
Let your child soak, squeeze, and pause as they like.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A contained sensory moment with a little splash and easy outdoor cleanup. Use a small amount of water and stop while it still feels good.
playIdeas.parentNote: Using just a small amount of water helps the activity stay light.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Choose a non-slippery surface and supervise around water.

playIdeas.title: Chair train pretend
playIdeas.summary: Line up a couple of chairs for a small pretend train ride.
steps: Place two chairs in a short line.
Choose who or what is taking the train ride.
Pretend to start, stop, and arrive at one simple destination.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: This can feel exciting, so a little structure helps it stay calm. Set a gentle pace and keep the route short.
playIdeas.parentNote: You do not need a long storyline to make the train feel real.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use sturdy chairs and stay close so climbing and leaning stay safe.

playIdeas.title: Calm hand tracing
playIdeas.summary: Trace hands slowly on paper or in the air for a quiet settling moment.
steps: Place a hand on the table or in your lap.
Trace around the fingers slowly with a crayon or fingertip.
Pause to notice the shape and trace once more if it feels good.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A very simple quiet idea for a moment that needs soft edges. Trace slowly and let one outline be enough.
playIdeas.parentNote: Tracing in the air works too if paper feels like too much.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use age-safe drawing tools and supervise closely with younger children.

playIdeas.title: Toy wash station
playIdeas.summary: Wash a few sturdy toys with water and a cloth or sponge.
steps: Choose one or two washable toys.
Dip the cloth or sponge in a little water.
Wipe the toys slowly and set them aside to dry.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Practical-life play with a gentle sensory feel and a contained reset afterward. Use only a couple of toys so it stays manageable.
playIdeas.parentNote: The wiping matters more than getting the toys perfectly clean.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use only a small amount of water and choose toys without batteries or electronics.

playIdeas.title: Napkin folding helper
playIdeas.summary: Fold a few napkins together for a calm table helper moment.
steps: Place a small stack of napkins on the table.
Show one simple fold in half.
Let your child try folding, stacking, or smoothing them.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A quiet helper activity with almost no preparation. A small stack keeps the rhythm calm and easy.
playIdeas.parentNote: Crooked folds are fine; the rhythm is more important than the result.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use clean cloth or paper napkins and keep the area dry.

playIdeas.title: Animal sound pause
playIdeas.summary: Take turns making one gentle animal sound at a time.
steps: Choose one animal together, like a cat or duck.
Make the sound once in a gentle voice.
Pause to listen before choosing another animal.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Connection stays simple when the sounds are gentle and spaced out. The pause between animals helps the moment stay calm.
playIdeas.parentNote: You can stop after one or two animals if that feels best.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep voices soft and avoid animal jumps or rough movement in small spaces.

playIdeas.title: Quiet basket rotation
playIdeas.summary: Bring out one small basket of calm toys and rotate it for a fresh pause.
steps: Choose one basket with only a few calm items.
Set it down and let your child explore in their own order.
Put it away when the quiet moment feels finished.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A touch of novelty without more clutter or stimulation. Keep the basket small so the choice feels gentle.
playIdeas.parentNote: Rotating only one basket at a time helps the room feel calmer too.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use safe, familiar toys without loose parts for your child's age.

playIdeas.title: Big-small household match
playIdeas.summary: Match one big household item with one small one in simple pairs.
steps: Place one big and one small version of two household items nearby.
Name big and small once or twice.
Let your child match, compare, or line them up.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: An easy home activity that stays light and tidy. Guide a little, then step back and watch what your child notices.
playIdeas.parentNote: Two simple pairs are plenty to hold the idea together.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use safe household items without sharp edges or breakable parts.

playIdeas.title: Blanket cave reading
playIdeas.summary: Drape a blanket over a low spot for a tiny reading nook.
steps: Drape a light blanket over a low safe surface or your knees.
Bring one book inside or beside the blanket.
Read a page or two, or simply sit together in the small space.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A cozy reading nook with only a little setup. Keep the cave open and airy so the moment stays comfortable.
playIdeas.parentNote: Looking at the cover together can be enough for today.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Keep blankets light, openings visible, and never block a child inside the space.

playIdeas.title: Spoon mirror tap
playIdeas.summary: Tap a spoon softly beside a mirror and notice the sound and reflection.
steps: Stand or sit near the mirror together.
Tap the spoon gently against your hand or sink edge.
Watch the movement in the reflection and keep the sound soft.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A tiny sensory-observation moment that works best with a gentle pace. One or two soft taps may be plenty.
playIdeas.parentNote: Soft taps keep the activity interesting without making it sharp or loud.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Avoid tapping directly on glass and keep the area dry and supervised.

playIdeas.title: Pretend shop with cups
playIdeas.summary: Turn a few cups into a tiny pretend shop for serving and choosing.
steps: Set two or three cups on the table like shop items.
Invite your child to choose, serve, or pretend to sell one.
Take turns asking for one simple thing from the shop.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Gentle pretend play that feels social without needing many props. Keep the choices few so the scene stays calm.
playIdeas.parentNote: You can let your child lead the whole shop after the first turn.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use unbreakable cups and keep the play surface stable.

playIdeas.title: Outdoor leaf noticing
playIdeas.summary: Notice a few leaves outdoors and talk about shape, color, or texture.
steps: Choose a safe outdoor place with leaves or plants nearby.
Pick up or point to one leaf at a time.
Notice color, size, or texture together without rushing.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A calm outside pause for lower-energy moments. A minute or two of noticing can be enough.
playIdeas.parentNote: The quiet pace is part of what makes this useful.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Stay on safe ground and avoid unfamiliar plants.

playIdeas.title: Bath toy rescue
playIdeas.summary: Rescue one bath toy at a time from a small bowl or bath edge.
steps: Place one bath toy in a small bowl or at the bath edge.
Invite your child to scoop or lift it out.
Let the toy go back in and rescue it again if they want.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: Bath play stays simple and focused with one toy at a time. Expect a little splash and an easy reset.
playIdeas.parentNote: One toy is enough to make the rescue feel real.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Stay within arm's reach in the bath and keep water play small.

playIdeas.title: Clean cloth wipe helper
playIdeas.summary: Offer a clean cloth for wiping one safe surface together.
steps: Choose one small safe surface, like a table edge or tray.
Show one slow wiping motion.
Let your child wipe a little, then stop while it still feels good.
playIdeas.whatToExpect: A tiny household task can become a steady, connected moment. Keeping the surface small helps it feel calming instead of like work.
playIdeas.parentNote: A few slow wipes can make the helper role feel real.
playIdeas.safetyNote: Use only water or a plain damp cloth and avoid cleaning products during play.

sounds.title: Soft rain
sounds.summary: Gentle rain for a calmer background.

sounds.title: Warm noise
sounds.summary: A steady warm noise for quieter routines.

sounds.title: Quiet stream
sounds.summary: Soft flowing water for a peaceful pause.

sounds.title: Evening crickets
sounds.summary: A calm evening sound for winding down.

sounds.title: Room fan
sounds.summary: A soft fan sound for steady background calm.

sounds.title: Dishwasher hum
sounds.summary: A gentle household hum for everyday routines.
